_comment: SKELETON, not data. `status: skeleton` makes `arm_runner.py run` refuse this plan (exit 2),
and the referenced pack is itself `status: draft`. Both must be frozen before a real run: the
plan because its arms and rounds define the comparison, the pack because its intent groups are
the construction truth the primary indicator is scored against.
The tasks come from the pack, not from this file. Keeping them in one place means the labels
the truth-consistency checks are performed against are the same text the sessions actually run;
duplicating the text here would let the two drift apart silently.
Topology is 'in-process-multi-session' because A3/A4 need it and nothing weaker will do:
`ledgerScope: 'cross-session'` reads the governor instance's IN-MEMORY event list, and the
ledger file is append-only with no read-back path. N separate `dsh` processes sharing a ledger
directory therefore cannot see each other (review R4.3), so under 'multi-process' the treatment
never fires and a null result cannot be distinguished from broken wiring. `arm_runner.py`
refuses A3/A4 under 'multi-process' for exactly that reason.
dsh.profile is 'coord-inproc', NOT the shipped 'headless' profile: 'headless' mounts a one-shot
runner that consumes one task at startup, while the in-process backend needs a leaf that mounts
dsh-base's core (agent, agent-loop, session, llm-deepseek, fs, sandbox) WITHOUT that runner.
The round driver then creates every session of the round through the one shared `ctx.agents`
registry. Creating that profile on the machine is the remaining live step; see harness/README.md.
